result:
I'd dissolve the gap between how people actually experience life and what they believe about people different from them.

Most cruelty comes from abstraction—hating a group you've never encountered, fearing what you've only heard about. But direct encounter tends to scramble those neat categories. You can't quite hate someone once you know their specific fears, or what makes them laugh.

I think almost everything else—justice, innovation, basic cooperation—becomes more possible once that gap closes. Not perfectly. People with full understanding can still disagree sharply. But the poisonous distance collapses.

I don't know if it's even achievable at scale. But if I could dial one thing, that's the dial I'd turn.
